# Transforming data on fetch

Transform requests in [getRequestInit()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#getRequestInit) and responses in
[parseResponse()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#parseResponse), on a base class when every endpoint needs it. Use
[process()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#process) for one endpoint's result, such as adding a value from its arguments, and
[Entity.process()](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#process) for one Entity's fields wherever it appears.

> **Tip**
>
> If you control the API, change the data it sends instead. A thin client is faster and simpler. Use these transforms
> for APIs you do not control.

## Snakes to camels

Many APIs use `snake_case` keys. To use `camelCase` in TypeScript, transform the keys in both directions. A base class
converts responses in [parseResponse()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#parseResponse), not `process()`, because
[resource()](./resource.vue.md)'s `delete` sets its own `process()`, which replaces the class's.

```typescript title="CamelResource.ts"
import { camelCase, snakeCase } from 'lodash';
import { RestEndpoint, RestGenerics } from '@data-client/rest';

function deeplyApplyKeyTransform(obj: any, transform: (key: string) => string) {
  const ret: Record<string, any> = Array.isArray(obj) ? [] : {};
  Object.keys(obj).forEach(key => {
    if (obj[key] != null && typeof obj[key] === 'object') {
      ret[transform(key)] = deeplyApplyKeyTransform(obj[key], transform);
    } else {
      ret[transform(key)] = obj[key];
    }
  });
  return ret;
}

class CamelEndpoint<O extends RestGenerics = any> extends RestEndpoint<O> {
  getRequestInit(body) {
    // we'll need to do the inverse operation when sending data back to the server
    if (body) {
      return super.getRequestInit(deeplyApplyKeyTransform(body, snakeCase));
    }
    return super.getRequestInit(body);
  }
  async parseResponse(response) {
    const value = await super.parseResponse(response);
    // a 204 response has no body
    return value && deeplyApplyKeyTransform(value, camelCase);
  }
}
```

## Deserializing fields

JSON has few types, so APIs send many values as strings. Examples are [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)
dates and high-precision decimals ([floats can be lossy](https://floating-point-gui.de/)). Strings are fine to display.
To compute with them, such as adding time to a date or multiplying two numbers, deserialize them.

Use [Entity.schema](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#schema) with [Temporal.Instant](https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/) and
[BigNumber](https://github.com/MikeMcl/bignumber.js):

```tsx title="api/Price"
import { Entity, RestEndpoint } from '@data-client/rest';
import { Temporal } from 'temporal-polyfill';
import BigNumber from 'bignumber.js';

export class ExchangePrice extends Entity {
  exchangePair = '';
  updatedAt = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(0);
  price = new BigNumber(0);
  pk() {
    return this.exchangePair;
  }
  static key = 'ExchangePrice';

  static schema = {
    updatedAt: Temporal.Instant.from,
    price: BigNumber,
  };
}
export const getPrice = new RestEndpoint({
  path: '/price/:exchangePair',
  schema: ExchangePrice,
});
```

```html title="PricePage.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useSuspense } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { getPrice } from './api/Price';

  const currentPrice = await useSuspense(getPrice, {
    exchangePair: 'btc-usd',
  });
</script>

<template>
  <dl class="stats">
    <div>
      <dt>
        {{ currentPrice.exchangePair.toUpperCase() }}, as of
        <time>
          {{ currentPrice.updatedAt.toLocaleString('en-US', { dateStyle: 'medium' }) }}
        </time>
      </dt>
      <dd>${{ currentPrice.price.toFormat(2) }}</dd>
    </div>
  </dl>
</template>
```

### Deserializing Date

To use the legacy [Date](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date),
wrap its constructor in a function [schema](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/schema).

```ts
export class ExchangePrice extends Entity {
  exchangePair = '';
  updatedAt = new Date(0);
  price = new BigNumber(0);
  pk() {
    return this.exchangePair;
  }
  static key = 'ExchangePrice';

  static schema = {
    updatedAt: iso => new Date(iso),
    price: BigNumber,
  };
}
```

## Case of the missing `Id`

Some APIs leave the primary key out of the response. For example, `https://mystreamsite.tv/[username]/` returns a
stream without its `username`, which is the stream's only unique identifier.

Add the `username` from the endpoint's arguments in [RestEndpoint.process()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#process).

```json title="GET https://mystreamsite.tv/ntucker/"
{
  "title": "When I'm Grandmaster, I will play faster.",
  "game": "Starcraft II",
  "current_viewers": 1337,
  "live": true
}
```

```typescript title="api/Stream.ts"
class Stream extends Entity {
  username = '';
  title = '';
  game = '';
  currentViewers = 0;
  live = false;

  pk() {
    return this.username;
  }
  static key = 'Stream';
}

const getStream = new RestEndpoint({
  urlPrefix: 'https://mystreamsite.tv',
  path: '/:username',
  schema: Stream,
  process(value, { username }) {
    value.username = username;
    return value;
  },
});
```

### Ticker prices

Coinbase's ticker response does not include its primary key `product_id`.
[RestEndpoint.process()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#process) adds it from the `productId` argument.

```typescript title="Ticker" {29-32}
import { Entity, RestEndpoint } from '@data-client/rest';
import { Temporal } from 'temporal-polyfill';

export class Ticker extends Entity {
  product_id = '';
  trade_id = 0;
  price = 0;
  size = '0';
  time = Temporal.Instant.fromEpochMilliseconds(0);
  bid = '0';
  ask = '0';
  volume = '';

  pk(): string {
    return this.product_id;
  }
  static key = 'Ticker';

  static schema = {
    price: Number,
    time: Temporal.Instant.from,
  };
}

export const getTicker = new RestEndpoint({
  urlPrefix: 'https://api.exchange.coinbase.com',
  path: '/products/:productId/ticker',
  schema: Ticker,
  process(value, { productId }) {
    value.product_id = productId;
    return value;
  },
  pollFrequency: 2000,
});
```

```html title="AssetPrice.vue" {8}
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useLive } from '@data-client/vue';
  import NumberFlow from '@number-flow/vue';
  import { getTicker } from './Ticker';

  const props = defineProps<{ productId: string }>();

  const ticker = await useLive(getTicker, () => ({
    productId: props.productId,
  }));
</script>

<template>
  <dl class="stats">
    <div>
      <dt>{{ productId }}</dt>
      <dd>
        <NumberFlow
          :value="ticker.price"
          :format="{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }"
        />
      </dd>
    </div>
  </dl>
</template>
```

### Key in a nested object

Some APIs put the primary key inside a nested object, such as `{ post: { id }, creator, saved }`. Copy it
to a top-level `id` in [Entity.process()](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#process), so lookups take `{ id }`. See
[Primary key in a nested object](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#primary-key-in-a-nested-object) for the example.

## Using HTTP Headers

To read HTTP [Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Headers), override
[RestEndpoint.parseResponse()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#parseResponse). It receives the fetch
[Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response). For example, cursor-based
[pagination](./pagination.vue.md#tokens-in-http-headers) can send its cursor in a header.

```typescript
import { RestEndpoint, RestGenerics } from '@data-client/rest';

class GithubEndpoint<
  O extends RestGenerics = any,
> extends RestEndpoint<O> {
  async parseResponse(response: Response) {
    const results = await super.parseResponse(response);
    if (
      (response.headers && response.headers.has('link')) ||
      Array.isArray(results)
    ) {
      return {
        link: response.headers.get('link'),
        results,
      };
    }
    return results;
  }
}
```

## File download {#file-download}

For endpoints that return binary data (files, images, PDFs), set
[`content: 'blob'`](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#content). The return type is `Blob` and
`schema` defaults to `undefined` (binary data isn't normalizable). Use `dataExpiryLength: 0`
to avoid caching large blobs in memory.

```typescript title="downloadFile.ts"
import { RestEndpoint } from '@data-client/rest';

export const downloadFile = new RestEndpoint({
  path: '/files/:id/download',
  content: 'blob',
  dataExpiryLength: 0,
});
```

```html title="DownloadButton.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
  import { useController } from '@data-client/vue';
  import { downloadFile } from './downloadFile';

  const props = defineProps<{ id: string }>();
  const ctrl = useController();

  const handleDownload = async () => {
    const blob: Blob = await ctrl.fetch(downloadFile, { id: props.id });
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.download = 'download';
    a.click();
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
  };
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="handleDownload">Download</button>
</template>
```

To extract the filename from the `Content-Disposition` header, override
[parseResponse](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#parseResponse):

```typescript title="downloadFile.ts"
import { RestEndpoint } from '@data-client/rest';

export const downloadFile = new RestEndpoint({
  path: '/files/:id/download',
  content: 'blob',
  dataExpiryLength: 0,
  async parseResponse(response) {
    const blob = await response.blob();
    const disposition = response.headers.get('Content-Disposition');
    const filename =
      disposition?.match(/filename="?(.+?)"?$/)?.[1] ?? 'download';
    return { blob, filename };
  },
  process(value): { blob: Blob; filename: string } {
    return value;
  },
});
```

For `ArrayBuffer` responses (useful for processing binary data in-memory), use
`content: 'arrayBuffer'` the same way.

## Name calling

To rename a key the API uses, map it in both directions: the Entity's [process()](https://dataclient.io/rest/api/Entity#process) renames it
in every response that contains the Entity, including lists and nested data, and the endpoint's
[getRequestInit()](./RestEndpoint.vue.md#getRequestInit) renames it back in request bodies. Components then use only
your name.

```typescript title="Article.ts"
import { Entity, RestEndpoint, RestGenerics } from '@data-client/rest';

export class Article extends Entity {
  id = '';
  carrotsUsed = 0;

  static process(value: any, parent: any, key: string, args: any[]) {
    const { carrotsUsedIsThisNameTooLong, ...rest } = super.process(
      value,
      parent,
      key,
      args,
    );
    return carrotsUsedIsThisNameTooLong === undefined ? rest : (
        { ...rest, carrotsUsed: carrotsUsedIsThisNameTooLong }
      );
  }
}

export class RenamedEndpoint<
  O extends RestGenerics = any,
> extends RestEndpoint<O> {
  getRequestInit(body: any) {
    if (body && 'carrotsUsed' in body) {
      const { carrotsUsed, ...rest } = body;
      return super.getRequestInit({
        ...rest,
        carrotsUsedIsThisNameTooLong: carrotsUsed,
      });
    }
    return super.getRequestInit(body);
  }
}
```
